comparison: C wrapper normalized vs Rust/Kornia minimal candidates, projective Frobenius distance threshold 1e-6
conclusion: The C wrapper formula is correct: its normalized candidate matrices preserve the input constraints and its denormalized matrices preserve pixel residuals. The discrepancy is the legacy pydegensac partial-pivot RREF null-space gauge, whose coordinates are 200-1600 despite a well-conditioned normalized design. It magnifies Cardano/root-combination roundoff, leaving rank-three residual singular values around 1e-9. Rust's orthonormal Householder null space and Kornia's reparameterized pencil agree. This is not a Rust solver regression and must not be used as a strict normalized-C parity requirement.
